name: AI implementation retainer for SMBs
one_liner: Build AI automations and voice agents for small and mid-sized businesses as a paid setup plus a monthly retainer, starting from a paid AI audit.
customer: Owners of small and mid-sized businesses, for example investment firms, that don't know how to use AI
offer: A paid AI audit to get in the door, then custom automations, voice agents and internal apps built with Claude and no-code tools, plus ongoing part-time consulting
how_it_makes_money: Setup fee plus monthly retainer. In one real case it was $3,500 setup plus $1,500/month for 6 months. A larger 6-month consulting contract was worth $50,000. The suggested model is $1-5K/month after a paid audit.
startup_cost: low (AI tool subscriptions only; no amount stated)
time_to_first_revenue: Weeks. The first deal came from a pitch to someone already in his network.
evidence: '$3,500 for setup and then $1,500 a month for six months' - 9DyLtQEDXN0
About 12 hours to build the $3,500 app, then about 1.5 hours a month to maintain it - 9DyLtQEDXN0
'the contract that he gave me for the first six months... was for $50,000' - 9DyLtQEDXN0
Pitched model: 'do AI audits for a fee... then charge one to five K a month' - 6u7tkj7UJvs
risks: Sales calls and building trust are needed, so it is not fully async
Crowded market with 'AI agency' sellers
The first clients usually come from your own network, which is hard to repeat
The founder said he had no coding background, so delivery quality can vary

name: Niche AI micro-SaaS (FormulaBot model)
one_liner: A no-code, AI-built tool that solves one repeated work problem, such as writing Excel formulas, sold as a freemium subscription.
customer: Office workers and analysts who struggle with a specific tool (Excel in this case)
offer: A chatbot-style add-on that generates formulas and analyses spreadsheet data
how_it_makes_money: Freemium SaaS priced from $0 to $35/month. FormulaBot makes about $26K/month.
startup_cost: low (Bubble or other AI app builder subscription)
time_to_first_revenue: unknown; months of marketing were needed
evidence: FormulaBot 'is now making around $26,000 per month', built by a non-programmer using Bubble - 9UevzmCNpw0
'pricing plans range anywhere from zero to $35 per month' - 9UevzmCNpw0
'David put in a ton of effort in marketing' - 9UevzmCNpw0
Validate before building: money already changing hands for a problem is the best proof of demand; get a 'smallest paid promise' (pre-sale) first - Bc-Hw9__7-Y
risks: 'On Monday, nobody buys it' - building is easy, distribution is hard
Copycat products and changes to the underlying AI or platforms
Slow to reach meaningful MRR

name: Cake-drop outbound gifting for sales teams
one_liner: A middleman service that sends custom cakes from partner bakeries to a sales team's prospects to win meetings.
customer: B2B sales teams and enterprise sales organisations
offer: Cakes with a custom message, delivered to target prospects and fulfilled by local partner bakeries
how_it_makes_money: Charge per cake (about $80) and keep the margin over the bakery's price. Daymaker reportedly does about $4K/day in revenue at about 30% margin.
startup_cost: low (no inventory; bakery partnerships plus a website)
time_to_first_revenue: unknown; likely weeks once bakery partners are signed
evidence: daymaker.com is 'doing around $4,000 a day in revenue... 30% margins' - AdMZ3eW4WsA
'at 80 bucks a cake'; napkin math of about $1,000 per customer won at a 33% meeting conversion rate - AdMZ3eW4WsA
The founder doesn't bake: 'has the bakeries send them out and just plays as a middle man' - AdMZ3eW4WsA
risks: Quality control across many bakeries
Delivery logistics for perishable products
A UK version needs its own network of bakery partners
Easy to copy

name: Recurring employee-birthday cake service for HR
one_liner: A subscription where HR departments have a cake sent automatically for each employee's birthday through partner bakeries.
customer: HR and people teams at companies
offer: Automatic birthday or recognition cakes, scheduled from an employee list
how_it_makes_money: Recurring per-cake billing with a margin over the bakery's cost (no exact figures given)
evidence: The Daymaker founder's original business: 'cake dropshipping... HR departments on recurring billing... every time somebody in their department has a birthday' - AdMZ3eW4WsA (weak: no revenue stated)
risks: Weak evidence: no revenue or pricing given
Companies may cut perk budgets
Same fulfilment risks as the sales-gifting version

name: Niche audio podcast with paid ad-free subscription
one_liner: A podcast that serves a specific listener need (here, bedtime stories to help people sleep) and earns money from a premium subscription.
offer: Free podcast episodes plus a paid tier with ad-free or bonus episodes
how_it_makes_money: About 13-14K subscribers at $40/year, which is over $500K/year, plus ads and other income streams
time_to_first_revenue: Long. The show reached 10M downloads after about a year, and paid subscriptions came later.
evidence: 'north of 13,000, 14,000 subscribers... At $40 a year, that's over half a million dollars' - AyMm_Tl5vXM
'About a year in, we had already hit 10 million downloads'; an Apple 'New and Noteworthy' feature helped - AyMm_Tl5vXM
risks: Hit-driven: one success can't be assumed for others
Slow to monetise
Sleep audio is a crowded category
A Portuguese-language version is an untested idea, not something shown in the transcript

name: Gourmet mushroom micro-farm
one_liner: Grow gourmet mushrooms at home and sell them at farmers' markets and to local buyers.
customer: Farmers' market shoppers and local restaurants
how_it_makes_money: Direct sales. Up to $10K/month at peak season, and $1,000 in a single day at one market.
startup_cost: low (shelving racks, a pond fogger and grow supplies; no total stated)
time_to_first_revenue: unknown; a few weeks of growing cycles
evidence: 'at peak season, it makes up to $10,000 a month' - 6WS5C9u-ak0
'I made a thousand dollars in a day selling at my local farmer's market' - 6WS5C9u-ak0
risks: Physical, hands-on work
Contamination risk
Revenue is seasonal
Poor fit for someone with limited time who wants async work

name: Amazon returns pallet flipping
one_liner: Buy pallets of Amazon customer returns and resell the items one by one.
offer: Returned goods such as chainsaws, ice makers and slushy makers
how_it_makes_money: Arbitrage. A pallet cost $700, with individual items listed at $110-$359 retail. The resale outcome was not stated.
evidence: 'I paid $700 for this palette'; items included a $110 chainsaw and a $359 slushy maker - 9YvVg2ljGYY
'a lot of the products seemed kind of cheap, some broken, questionable whether I could really sell' - 9YvVg2ljGYY (weak evidence)
risks: Broken or unsellable stock
Storage space and lots of manual work
Retail prices quoted are not actual sale prices
Margins are unproven
